title.value: Forgetting Enhances Episodic Control With Structured Memories
title.justification: The paper focuses on the role of forgetting in enhancing decision-making through structured memories, specifically through the lens of reinforcement learning.
title.quote: Yalnizyan-Carson A and Richards BA (2022) Forgetting Enhances Episodic Control With Structured Memories. Front. Comput. Neurosci. 16:757244.

extractions.description: This study explores the hypothesis that forgetting can enhance performance in decision-making by utilizing structured episodic memories. Using a reinforcement learning framework, the research shows that an agent employing episodic memory can forget a significant portion of older memories while maintaining or even improving performance. By employing structured mnemonic representations, the agent minimizes the impact of outdated or infrequently used information, leading to more consistent and efficient decision-making. The paper provides theoretical support for the idea that forgetting is beneficial for episodic control systems and decision-making.

primary_category.justification: The paper is primarily focused on cognitive science and reinforcement learning principles related to memory and decision-making without direct reference to ecological or sustainable applications.
primary_category.quote: This work offers a putative explanation for how active forgetting in biological brains may present advantages over a memory system that can store all events ever experienced.

secondary_categories.justification: Despite being interdisciplinary with some application potential in AI, the paper lacks direct relevance to eco-responsible AI as it doesn't focus on environmental or sustainable applications.
secondary_categories.quote: Therefore, to determine the validity of the beneficial forgetting hypothesis, we used an episodic control agent trained to forage for rewards in a series of maze environments.

primary_sub_category.justification: The study does not fall into a specific eco-responsible sub-category as defined in the list, focusing instead on reinforcement learning and cognitive mechanisms.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our analyses of the agents show that forgetting reduces the influence of outdated information and states which are not frequently visited on the policies produced by the episodic control system.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper does not align with any of the eco-responsible sub-categories as it deals primarily with episodic memory and cognitive reinforcement learning strategies.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We first investigated the effects of memory restriction on performance in four gridworld tasks for agents using either structured or unstructured representations of state information.
